chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, in his book, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought a sheep for his 'mut'ah (temporary sacrifice for Eid or Hajj), and it was stolen from him or perished, he said: 'If he had secured it in its saddle (or place of security) and it was lost, it has counted for him.'

key_terms.أَوْثَقَهَا: He secured it / tied it firmly
key_terms.مُتْعَتِهِ: His temporary sacrifice (referring to the specific sacrificial animal for Eid al-Adha or Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a sacrificial animal is stolen or dies after purchase?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *khuruj al-wajib* (exemption from obligation) in *Tamattu' Hajj* when the sacrificial animal is lost or stolen despite the owner's reasonable precaution (*awthaha*). It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness, ensuring that the pilgrim is not penalized for circumstances beyond their control, thereby fulfilling the divine command without undue hardship.
